subject: Re: Acme — Invoice estimate & cost model
messages:
From: Alice Thompson <alice.thompson@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Li <devon.li@acme.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Acme discovery follow-up / token volumes

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the call earlier — helpful framing. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we try to finalize budget and compare unit economics: 

- Avg prompt + response per interaction: ~3k tokens (prompt 1k, response 2k)
- Estimated monthly active users for initial rollout: 25k MAU
- Expected interactions per MAU/day: 2
- Heavy tail: top 10% users may be 5x the average usage

Can you confirm what the expected $/1M tokens would look like across the pricing tiers you discussed (hosted vs dedicated vs private)? Also, please attach a simple invoice estimate and cost model so our finance team can run it. Budget range: we're looking to keep initial runtime costs under $30k/mo if possible.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Thompson
Director, Product — Acme Corp
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thompson <alice.thompson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery follow-up / token volumes

Hi Alice — great to speak earlier, appreciate the details. Attaching three artifacts: a one-page invoice estimate (acme_invoice_estimate_v3.xlsx), the raw token-breakdown CSV we used to build the calc (acme_cost_model_v2.csv), and a sanitized pricing calculator PDF (redwood_pricing_calculator.pdf). Those are included in the Drive link I shared as well.

Quick summary (high level):
- Your baseline estimate: ~25k MAU * 2 interactions/day * 3k tokens/interactions * 30 days = 4.5B tokens/month
- Host / shared (standard hosted tier) list-rate: ~$0.60 / 1k tokens => ~$2,700 / 1M tokens (note: list rates vary by model family; discounts applied for committed usage)
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) unit economics we can achieve with a 6–12 month commit: ~$0.50 / 1k tokens => ~$500 / 1M tokens (after discounts / batching / KV cache savings this typically drops further for heavy steady workloads)
- Private on-prem (customer-managed infra): unit cost can be lower depending on infra amortization; we provide an estimate template in the spreadsheet.

Important notes:
- The hosted list-rate above is the retail API price; it includes model cost, serving, and infra margin. For deals with committed capacity we can get you into the $400–$800 / 1M tokens band depending on model variant and quantization.
- For 4.5B tokens/mo, target unit economics to hit $30k/mo would require ~$6.6 / 1M tokens (which is unrealistic at this scale given model compute cost). That suggests we need to either: reduce token volume (prompt engineering, caching, summarization), change SLA/latency targets for cheaper model variants, or structure a reserved capacity & caching plan to lower cost significantly.

I've called out the rows in the attached XLSX where you can toggle model family (base vs f16-quantized variant), batching assumptions, and prefix cache hit % to see sensitivity on $/1M tokens.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll add a conservative 3 scenarios tab in the spreadsheet: conservative / expected / aggressive.
2) Can you confirm whether Acme would consider a 6–12 month reserved commit (yes/no)? That materially changes the units.
3) If you can share a representative prompt-set (10–20 examples) we can run a more targeted cost sim and show caching benefits.

I’ll follow up with the revised spreadsheet (scenarios) by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Devon Li <devon.li@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Alice Thompson <alice.thompson@acme.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery follow-up / token volumes

Thanks Sean. A couple of clarifying questions after scanning the workbook:

- The top-line tokens calc says 4.5B tokens/month — is that accounting for caching? If we get a 30% prefix/KV cache hit rate that would materially drop effective billable tokens, right?
- For the dedicated example you listed $0.50 / 1k tokens (~$500 / 1M). Can you show a worked example of how batching and cache reduce that to the $300–$400 / 1M band you referenced?
- Our procurement team asked whether you can provide a one-page invoice we can present — ideally with an itemized line for committed throughput and one for overage.

We are open to a committed option if the math lines up — 6 months is preferable.

—Devon
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Devon Li <devon.li@acme.com>, Alice Thompson <alice.thompson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery follow-up / token volumes

Devon / Alice — thanks, and great questions. Short answers and attached deliverables.

1) Cache: the baseline 4.5B is raw tokens assuming no cache. In the spreadsheet I added a cache sensitivity table; at 30% prefix/KV cache hit the billable tokens drop to ~3.15B (same interaction counts). We also model an effective 15% reduction from batching (amortized per-token cost improvement) for the dedicated pool in the conservative scenario.

2) Worked example (conservative dedicated scenario) — all numbers per 1M billable tokens:
- Raw dedicated compute cost (model runtime w/ quantization): $320 / 1M tokens
- Serving infra + orchestration + margin: $80 / 1M tokens
- Caching & batching benefit (conservative amortization): -$60 / 1M tokens
- Effective price to customer after a 12-month commit + volume discount: $340 / 1M tokens

So that lands in the $300–$400 / 1M band for committed dedicated capacity. The XLSX has a toggles sheet where you can move caching from 0–50% and commit term 0/6/12 to see the delta.

3) One-page invoice: attached (acme_invoice_estimate_v3.xlsx). It has two line items: 1) Reserved capacity (monthly commitment) with committed throughput and price, 2) Overage (billing per 1M billable tokens at the overage rate). I exported a PDF as well for procurement.

Suggested next steps:
- If Acme is comfortable, confirm a 6-month reserved commit (we’ll price it in the XLSX and produce a draft SOW).
- Share prompt examples and a short list of high-volume user flows so we can run a caching sim.
- I’ll set up a 30-minute math walk-through with your procurement + finance — Thursday or Friday this week.

We want to make sure the numbers are transparent for your finance team. Let me know which day/time works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
